subject: Evaluate code but do not markup

messages.author: f6fb090afa6ce6b2
messages.subject: Evaluate code but do not markup
parts:
Is there a clean way to evaluate all the code in a Rmd/Rnw/etc file without producing the markup?

I could purl(file.Rmd) and then source(file.R) but then I will have produced file.R which I don't really need and also this wouldn't take advantage of caching.  I could take advantage of caching by kniting file.Rmd but then I've produced file.md which I don't really need.

Thanks for any tips.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Evaluate code but do not markup
parts:
I apologize if I came across as complaining.  That certainly was not my intention.  I hope my actual question is clear, but if you need to know my motivation, it is this:

I want to add a feature to the Vim-R-plugin that will allow users to evaluate all the code in a Rmd, Rnw, etc file.  I think this would be especially useful in the case that a user is evaluating R code from some R chunks in, say, a main Rmd file and then comes to a chunk which is a child rmd file.  Rather than opening said child file and running the code within that file, the user might just want to evaluate all the R code in the child file at once.  Clearly, there is no need to produce markup or an R file for this scenario.   Sure, the markup can be produced and then deleted immediately, but I am sure you will agree this is not very clean (and why write to the hard drive if not necessary), especially if the functionality I am interested in is already available somehow in knitr.

Thanks.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Evaluate code but do not markup
parts:
I guess the easiest approach might be to write the output to a
temporary file or stdout(), e.g. knit('foo.Rmd', output = tempfile()).
Constructing the output markup is relatively cheap compared to
executing the R code chunks, so it may not be a bad idea to do it and
discard it.

Note that child documents do not produce file output -- only character
strings of the markup are returned, e.g. this will not produce
child-a.md if you put this child chunk in a main document:

```{r child='child-a.Rmd'}
```

Regards,
Yihui
